objectives:
	Participate actively and effectively in academic discussions and collaborative group interactions.
	Critically evaluate, synthesize, and communicate ideas from multiple English-language sources.
	Present information, opinions, and arguments clearly with appropriate evidence and supporting details.
	Analyze issues from multiple perspectives through critical thinking and evidence-based reasoning.
	Apply academic discussion strategies to express, justify, and respond to ideas in spoken English.
	Reflect on their own learning and continuously improve their academic communication skills.
content:
Topics to be discussed
Topic 1: Conversation
Q: What makes a conversation meaningful, and how can we become better communicators?
Topic 2: Building relationship
Q: How can I build and sustain relationships?
Topic 3: Academic group discussion & talk moves
Q: How can I sustain discussion?
Topic 4: Emotion & feelings
Q: Why am I anxious?
Topic 5: Personal management
Q: Who am I? What do I do?
Topic 6:  Media & tech
Q: How much do I control my relationship with social media?
books: Teacher-developed tutorials and worksheets provide guidance for self-paced learning and in-class discussions. Supplementary materials are drawn from high-quality authentic sources, including NPR, BBC, CNN, The New York Times, The Conversation, and Vox.
grading_policy:
Preview notes &in-class works 40%
Round-table presentation 20%
Panel discussion 25%
Learning portfolio 15%
